description.title: Bacterial, clinical or host-associated sample for Escherichia coli O157:H7 str. SAKAI (EHEC)
description.comment: Full genome sequenced type strain Escherichia coli O157:H7 str. SAKAI.  This strain is associated with Hamburger disease, which is caused by the contamination of meat products by enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC). The identifier O157:H7 refers to the serotype of EHEC, and reflects the specific antigenic markers found on the surface of the cell. EHEC attaches and effaces to cells in the large intestine.There are numerous differences that distinguish O157:H7 from K-12, hundreds of them associated with genomic islands in either strain, including at least 9 large PAIs in O157:H7 that encode virulence factors. A type III secretion system, the locus of enterocyte effacement, numerous toxins and adhesins, as well as fimbrial gene clusters and iron uptake systems are found in these PAIs. Pathogenicity genes are also found on the plasmid pO157. Escherichia coli O157:H7 strain Sakai. This strain of O157:H7 was isolated in a 1996 outbreak in Sakai, Japan.

description.title: Generic sample from Escherichia coli B171

assemblyInfo.comments:
Escherichia coli B171 is a member of the enteropathogenic E. coli (EPEC), EPEC2 subgroup. This strain was provided by Dr. James B. Kaper from the University of Maryland School of Medicine and the Center for Vaccine Development. EPEC is an important cause of diarrhea in the developing world. EPEC infection is limited to the small intestine. EPEC adhere to the epithelial surface and secrete effectors into the eukaryotic cell, causing cellular rearrangement such as pedestals and the formation of attaching and effacing lesions. This infection is often self-limiting, but in infants, elderly and immuno- compromised individuals, the infection can result in hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) or hemorrhagic colitis (HC). Other virulence factors of E. coli B171 include O111:NM, bundle forming pilus encoding plasmid EAF (GenBank Accession Number AB024946) and the LEE pathogenicity island.
The annotation was added by the NCBI Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline (PGAP). Information about PGAP can be found here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genome/annotation_prok/
